recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core follow-up is needed unless the work group later changes external NUCC code system handling or licensing guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-13076 asked FHIR core to include required codes/support for NUCC Provider Taxonomy because provider-taxonomy was defined but disabled in bindings.xml and valueset-use-context. The issue is Published with resolution Persuasive with Modification, and the final Jira comment says the existing references worked while NUCC expansions remained empty because the codes require a license.
initial_application: No source commit explicitly mentions FHIR-13076. The relevant source history came through the same UsageContext value-set work: 08d280b8e8593f627923e0cade06a02eea8d7d2b added provider-taxonomy in disabled/commented form for FHIR-13059, then 8b16115d880b33726d98fd973da248d688742494 enabled the ProviderTaxonomy binding, included http://nucc.org/provider-taxonomy in valueset-use-context, and fixed the system URI.
additional_context: FHIR-13059 is the closely related UsageContext value-set issue and is already represented on the combined branch by db1c1f1c44e569412eda2a28f3408646ca3802d3. Current source keeps the ProviderTaxonomy binding, provider-taxonomy ValueSet, valueset-use-context inclusion, and UsageContext user additional binding wired together. Confluence only supplied a tracker-call listing for FHIR-13076, and Zulip/Confluence searches found no conflicting community discussion.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already matches the final Jira understanding: provider taxonomy is actively referenced, but FHIR does not bundle an expanded NUCC code list.

related_jiras.note: The FHIR-13059 UsageContext value-set change introduced the provider-taxonomy files and references that FHIR-13076 discusses; it already has a combined-branch reconcile commit, so it was not republished here.
